name: Tile Matching Solitaire
description: Solitaire game using around 144 tiles (traditionally Mah Jong). Tiles are stacked in layers with horizontal rows; each row rests on the row below. Remove all tiles by taking matching pairs of exposed tiles (a tile is exposed when at the end of a row and not covered).

content.text: Solitaire game using around 144 tiles (traditionally Mah Jong). Tiles are stacked in layers with horizontal rows; each row rests on the row below. Remove all tiles by taking matching pairs of exposed tiles (a tile is exposed when at the end of a row and not covered).
Tile matching solitaire originated as a computer game and exists in many versions (e.g. Shanghai, Taipei, Kyodai), using Mah Jong or similar tiles in matching sets of four.
Single player. This solitaire is played by one person, who clears the layout by removing matching pairs of exposed tiles (tiles at the end of a row and not covered).
Set of around 144 tiles (Mah Jong traditionally).
Tiles are stacked in layers; each layer has horizontal rows. Tiles in a row rest on the row below. Remove pairs of exposed (uncovered) matching tiles until the layout is clear.

items.text: Mahjong Connect: Pairs of tiles can only be removed if they can be connected by a clear orthogonal path, often with not more than a given number of right-angle bends.
